citations.claim: pre-collision speed low, gap 0.005 to body 1, controller force ~6.5
intruder body fast approaching causing collision
post-collision speed jumped to 10.27, velocity reversed relative to waypoint
controller force 486.87 exceeds limit 72.67 at violating step 29, total energy 528.55

counterfactual.change: Removed the second (uncontrolled) colliding body, keeping all controller parameters and steps identical. Without collision impulse, velocity error stays small and force stays below fmax, proving collision-induced velocity jump is cause.

explanation: At step 28, controlled body 0 is almost touching fast body 1 (gap 0.005). The collision between 28-29 imparts large impulse, reversing velocity from ~2.9 m/s toward waypoint to ~10.3 m/s away. Controller's velocity-error law (kp * error) then commands force 486.8 N, far above fmax 72.67. Simulation does not clamp or re-check controller force after collision substeps, so the violation persists at final step. Removing the colliding body eliminates the velocity spike and violation.
vision_note: In steps 26-28 the large blue controller-driven body moves toward the green waypoint and comes into contact with the small red body directly above it at step 28. At step 29 the two bodies have collided and the controller-driven body is abruptly deflected to the southeast, away from the waypoint, while the red body recoils.
